chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al Maghra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who leases a land, then sub-leases it for more than what he leased it for, he said: There is no problem. This is not like the shop (hanut) nor the employee (ajir). Indeed, the excess of the employee and the shop is prohibited.

key_terms.الْأَجِيرِ: Employee or worker; referring to the sub-hiring of a worker for profit, which is prohibited.
key_terms.الْحَانُوتِ: Shop or store; a specific type of leased property where sub-leasing for profit is prohibited.
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: Prohibited; forbidden according to Islamic law.
key_terms.فَضْلَ: Excess or profit; the additional amount gained over the original cost.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sub-lease land for a profit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits sub-leasing land at a higher price, distinguishing it from the prohibited practices of sub-leasing a shop (hanut) or sub-hiring an employee (ajir). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the 'rent on rent' (rib al-rih) prohibition applies specifically to movable assets or labor where the intermediary adds no distinct utility, whereas land is treated as a stable asset where profit from sub-leasing is permissible.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn AbuUmeyr, from Abu Al Magra, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the man who leases a land, then he sub-leases it out with more than what he had leased it for. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem. This is not like the shops, nor like the employees (wages). The excess of the wages and the shops is Prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu al-Mighra’ who has said the following: “

About the case of a man who leases a piece of land, then rents it to someone for more than what he has leased for, he (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘It is not unlawful because it is not like a shop or wages; increase of wages and rent of shop is not lawful.’”
